citations.quote: Fix four-dimensional affine Minkowski spacetime with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, an inertial length-coordinate chart $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$, $x^0=ct$, and coordinates measured in metres, as specified by [[def-qft-framework-units]]. Write $\Box=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b$. The mass-shell parameter $\mu\ge0$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$ has the same unit. For a massive species, $\mu=m_{\mathrm{rest,SI}}c/\hbar$; $\mu=0$ is the separately admitted massless branch of the mathematical free-field construction. Thus $\hbar c\omega_\mu$ is physical energy and $\hbar\mathbf k$ is physical momentum. The natural-unit action is written $S/\hbar$. The scalar one-particle space is $\mathcal H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu;\mathbb C)$, where $H_\mu^+=\{(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k):\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3,\ \omega_\mu(\mathbf k)>0\}$ and $d\nu_\mu=d^3\mathbf k/((2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k))$; at $\mu=0$ the measure-zero apex $\mathbf k=0$ is omitted. These are the shell conventions of [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. For a smooth real classical scalar $\phi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb R$ with the canonical free-field length degree $-1$, adopt $$\frac{S_\phi}{\hbar}=-\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^4}\left(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\phi_{\mathrm n}\partial_b\phi_{\mathrm n}+\mu^2\phi_{\mathrm n}^2\right)\,d^4x.$$ For a smooth commuting classical Dirac spinor $\psi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb C^4$ with canonical free-field length degree $-3/2$, put $\bar\psi_{\mathrm n}=\psi_{\mathrm n}^\dagger\beta$ and use the Clifford convention $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$ from [[def-qft-framework-units]]. Adopt $$\frac{S_D}{\hbar}=\int_{\mathbb R^4}\bar\psi_{\mathrm n}(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi_{\mathrm n}\,d^4x.$$ The smooth classical variables in these functionals commute; no Grassmann algebra or path-integral construction is being adopted. These formulas specify local action densities: for arbitrary smooth global fields the total integrals need not converge. Only compactly supported variations are used; the action difference under such a variation is an integral over a compact set and is finite for smooth fields. With these variations on the fixed background, the intended Euler–Lagrange equations are $(\Box-\mu^2)\phi_{\mathrm n}=0$ and $(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi_{\mathrm n}=0$, conditional on the exact mathematical supplier recorded as [L1] below. As the physical interpretation of this selected free model, assign the real scalar species to the bosonic symmetric Fock representation and assign the Dirac field to the particle/antiparticle CAR representation on $\mathcal H_+\oplus\overline{\mathcal H_-}$. Choose the zero-particle Fock vectors as the scalar and Dirac vacuum states. This is an adopted species and statistics assignment. The CCR/CAR and operator properties of the specified representations are mathematical model consequences; they do not prove a general spin-statistics theorem or establish that nature realizes this model. The scalar construction is the Schwartz-smeared field $\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu\overline f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f)$ on the finite-particle domain, with the future-shell phase $p\circ x=\omega_\mu x^0-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x$, exactly as in [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. The Dirac construction is the bounded spacetime-smeared CAR field of [[lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality]], using the positive and negative projections of the specified free Dirac matrix. In that carrier, $\mathcal H_D=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k/(2\pi)^3;\mathbb C^4)$, $h_D(\mathbf k)=\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf k+\beta\mu$, and $P_\pm(\mathbf k)=(I_4\pm h_D(\mathbf k)/\omega_\mu(\mathbf k))/2$; the particle and antiparticle one-particle spaces are the closed ranges $\mathcal H_+$ and $\overline{\mathcal H_-}$. These carriers state their mathematical hypotheses and construction domains; their draft status is not an independent physics or proof approval. Tong's lecture notes and Srednicki's book draft provide independent presentations of the scalar and Dirac free-field formulations. Their formal mode notation supplies context for this adoption, not a proof of the operator-domain claims and not evidence that the adopted model describes nature.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following statement. > For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by > $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that > $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], let $\mu\ge0$, let $H_\mu$ and $K_\mu$ be as in [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]], and form $\mathcal F_s(H_\mu)$ with vacuum $\Omega$ and finite-particle domain $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ define on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ $$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu\overline f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f).$$ This is a complex-linear map of test functions into operators $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\to\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. For real $f$ it is symmetric and equals $\sqrt2\,\Phi_{\rm Segal}(K_\mu f)|_{\mathcal D_{\rm fin}}$, where the Segal field of [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]] is $\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=\overline{(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2}$. Thus its Weyl unitary is $W_\mu(f):=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2 K_\mu f)$ and, for real $f,g$, $$W_\mu(f)W_\mu(g)= e^{-i\,\operatorname{Im}\langle K_\mu f,K_\mu g\rangle_2}W_\mu(f+g).$$ For every real $f$ the vacuum Weyl expectation is $$\langle\Omega,W_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2 =e^{-\|K_\mu f\|_2^2/2}.$$ Here the inner product is second-variable-linear as fixed in [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. The vacuum has zero one-point function and two-point function $$\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(f)\Phi_\mu(g)\Omega\rangle_2 =\langle K_\mu\overline f,K_\mu g\rangle_2,$$ which obeys $\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(\overline f)\Phi_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2=\|K_\mu f\|_2^2\ge0$ for every complex test $f$ (ordinary diagonal positivity holds for real tests); higher vacuum moments of ordered real smeared fields obey the CCR pairing recursion and hence the free-field Wick pairing rule. The field is a weak operator-valued tempered distribution on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$: every matrix coefficient $f\mapsto\langle\Psi,\Phi_\mu(f)\Theta\rangle_2$ for $\Psi,\Theta\in\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is a continuous complex-linear functional on Schwartz space. Its adjoint satisfies $\Phi_\mu(f)^*|_{\mathcal D_{\rm fin}}=\Phi_\mu(\overline f)$, and its normalized vacuum defines a positive state on the finite polynomial $*$-algebra generated by these fields. The relative-coordinate two-point tempered distribution is $$W_\mu(z)=\int_{H_\mu^+}e^{-ip\circ z}\,d\nu_\mu(p),$$ understood by pairing with Schwartz tests. Its translation-invariant bidistribution is the shell integral of $e^{-ip\circ x}e^{ip\circ y}$; on product tests it is the displayed vacuum covariance. For $g=(a,\Lambda)$, let $f_g$ and $U_\mu(g)$ be the affine test pullback and one-particle action of [[lem-qft-scalar-poincare-action]]. Their Fock lifts implement the same covariance for $\Phi_\mu$ on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ and for the bounded Weyl operators. For translations, the joint spectral measure on Fock space is the second-quantized multiplier measure with one-particle vector $(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),-\mathbf k)$. Its support is contained in the closed future cone $\{(E,\mathbf P):E\ge|\mathbf P|\}$; the vacuum is an eigenvector at $(0,\mathbf0)$. These are conditional mathematical model deductions. No point field, empirical observation or measurement claim is made.

Assume Countable Choice. For $\mu\ge0$, define the tempered distribution $$\Delta_\mu(t,\mathbf x)= \int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3} \frac{\sin(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)t)}{\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)} e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x},$$ with the massless integrand defined off $\mathbf k=0$; its $1/|\mathbf k|$ behavior is locally integrable in three dimensions. Then $$\operatorname{supp}\Delta_\mu \subseteq\{(t,\mathbf x):t^2-|\mathbf x|^2\ge0\},$$ the closed causal cone for the $(-+++)$ metric. For real compactly supported smooth $f,g$, put $$\Delta_\mu(f,g)= \int_{\mathbb R^4}\!\int_{\mathbb R^4} f(x)g(y)\Delta_\mu(x-y)\,d^4x\,d^4y.$$ On $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ the smeared fields of [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]] satisfy $$[\Phi_\mu(f),\Phi_\mu(g)]=-i\Delta_\mu(f,g)I.$$ Consequently spacelike-separated supports give commuting fields.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite measure space and let $\boldsymbol\omega=(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_d):X\to\mathbb R^d$ be a finite-valued measurable map, where $d\ge1$. Put $H=L^2(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ with the second-variable-linear pairing of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]], and form the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(H)$. For $n\ge1$, identify $H_s^{(n)}$ with the symmetric subspace of $L^2(X^n,\overline{\mu^{\times n}};\mathbb C)$ by iterating [[lem-qft-l2-product-tensor-identification]]. Set $X^0=\{\star\}$, $s_0(\star)=0$, and for $n\ge1$ set $$s_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{r=1}^n\boldsymbol\omega(x_r)\in\mathbb R^d.$$ For $1\le j\le d$, define $H_j$ by multiplication by the $j$th coordinate $s_{n,j}$ on sector $n$, with exact domain $$D(H_j)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n): \sum_{n\ge1}\int_{X^n}|s_{n,j}|^2|\Psi_n|^2\,d\overline{\mu^{\times n}}<\infty\right\}.$$ Each $H_j$ is self-adjoint, and $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\cap D(H_j)$ is a graph core. The joint projection-valued measure [[def-projection-valued-measure]] on $\mathbb R^d$ is $$(E(B)\Psi)_n=\mathbf1_{s_n^{-1}(B)}\Psi_n\quad(n\ge1),\qquad (E(B)\Psi)_0=\mathbf1_B(0)\Psi_0.$$ For $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, let $H_\theta$ be multiplication on sector $n$ by $\theta\cdot s_n$, with its maximal square-integrability domain. Then $$U_\theta(t)\Psi:=\bigl(e^{it\theta\cdot s_n}\Psi_n\bigr)_{n\ge0}$$ is a strongly continuous unitary group on all of Fock space, and its norm derivative at zero exists exactly for $\Psi\in D(H_\theta)$, where it is $iH_\theta\Psi$. The zero-particle sector is the vacuum eigenvector at joint value $0$.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be open. For real $f\in C_c^\infty(O)$ define $$W_\mu(f):=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2K_\mu f),$$ where the Segal normalization is exactly $\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2$ on the finite-particle domain, as in [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. This scale makes the generator of $t\mapsto W_\mu(tf)$ equal to the real scalar field $\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f)$ of [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. Define the unital norm-closed operator algebra $$\mathfrak A_\mu(O)= \overline{\operatorname{alg}}^{\|\cdot\|} \{I,W_\mu(f),W_\mu(f)^*:f\in C_c^\infty(O;\mathbb R)\}.$$ Then $O_1\subseteq O_2$ implies $\mathfrak A_\mu(O_1)\subseteq\mathfrak A_\mu(O_2)$. If every difference $x-y$, with $x\in O_1$ and $y\in O_2$, is spacelike, then every element of $\mathfrak A_\mu(O_1)$ commutes with every element of $\mathfrak A_\mu(O_2)$. These are algebraic properties of the constructed representation; they are not empirical signaling or measurement claims.

Here $\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ is the Schwartz space of smooth complex functions whose coordinate-weighted derivatives are all bounded, as defined in [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]. Some QFT sources use its negative $(+---)$; the Lorentz group is unchanged, and the phase is fixed explicitly below. A parameter $\mu\ge0$ has inverse-length units and is only a mathematical shell parameter; it is not identified with a physical rest mass. u_\mu(p_\mu(\mathbf k))=  rac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)},\qquad H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d
u_\mu;\mathbb C),$$ where the omitted massless apex has measure zero. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ define its pointwise shell Fourier restriction by $$K_\mu f(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}f(x)e^{ip\circ x}\,d^4x.$$ The Fourier convention is exactly the displayed integral, with no prefactor. If $\widehat f(\xi^0, oldsymbol\xi)= \int f(x)e^{-2\pi i(x^0\xi^0+\mathbf x\cdot oldsymbol\xi)}\,d^4x$ denotes the standard transform in [[cor-fourier-transform-is-a-topological-automorphism-of-schwartz-space]], then $$\mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p):=\int f(x)e^{i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)}\,d^4x =\widehat f\!\left(- rac{p^0}{2\pi}, rac{\mathbf p}{2\pi}ight).$$ Its inverse is $$f(x)=(2\pi)^{-4}\int_{\mathbb R^4} \mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p)e^{-i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)} \,dp^0\,d^3\mathbf p.$$ Thus this convention is a time reflection and rescaling of the cited Schwartz automorphism and has the stated reciprocal normalization. The proper orthochronous Lorentz group consists of linear maps preserving $\eta$, orientation and the chosen future cone. A Poincare map is $x\mapsto a+\Lambda x$ with $a\in\mathbb R^4$ and $\Lambda$ in that group. This is a mathematical free scalar one-particle construction. It adopts the chosen coordinates, measure and Fourier convention; it asserts no experimental observation, physical mass identification or measurement outcome.

derivations.claim: The adopted scalar field is the defined complex-linear operator map on the common finite-particle domain.
The shell Fourier restriction annihilates the Klein–Gordon test operator, so both field coefficients vanish.
Vacuum covariance and positivity, Poincare covariance, and invariant vacuum follow from the inspected scalar carrier.
Causal support makes spacelike field commutators zero, and norm closure preserves Weyl-algebra commutation and isotony.
The sector-sum multiplier yields the exact self-adjoint Hamiltonian domain and the joint forward-cone spectrum.
The vacuum is the unique zero-energy vector; the massive threshold is hbar c mu and the massless positive spectrum has no gap.

citations.quote: Fix four-dimensional affine Minkowski spacetime with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, an inertial length-coordinate chart $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$, $x^0=ct$, and coordinates measured in metres, as specified by [[def-qft-framework-units]]. Write $\Box=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b$. The mass-shell parameter $\mu\ge0$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$ has the same unit. For a massive species, $\mu=m_{\mathrm{rest,SI}}c/\hbar$; $\mu=0$ is the separately admitted massless branch of the mathematical free-field construction. Thus $\hbar c\omega_\mu$ is physical energy and $\hbar\mathbf k$ is physical momentum. The natural-unit action is written $S/\hbar$. The scalar one-particle space is $\mathcal H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu;\mathbb C)$, where $H_\mu^+=\{(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k):\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3,\ \omega_\mu(\mathbf k)>0\}$ and $d\nu_\mu=d^3\mathbf k/((2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k))$; at $\mu=0$ the measure-zero apex $\mathbf k=0$ is omitted. These are the shell conventions of [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. For a smooth real classical scalar $\phi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb R$ with the canonical free-field length degree $-1$, adopt $$\frac{S_\phi}{\hbar}=-\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^4}\left(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\phi_{\mathrm n}\partial_b\phi_{\mathrm n}+\mu^2\phi_{\mathrm n}^2\right)\,d^4x.$$ For a smooth commuting classical Dirac spinor $\psi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb C^4$ with canonical free-field length degree $-3/2$, put $\bar\psi_{\mathrm n}=\psi_{\mathrm n}^\dagger\beta$ and use the Clifford convention $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$ from [[def-qft-framework-units]]. Adopt $$\frac{S_D}{\hbar}=\int_{\mathbb R^4}\bar\psi_{\mathrm n}(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi_{\mathrm n}\,d^4x.$$ The smooth classical variables in these functionals commute; no Grassmann algebra or path-integral construction is being adopted. These formulas specify local action densities: for arbitrary smooth global fields the total integrals need not converge. Only compactly supported variations are used; the action difference under such a variation is an integral over a compact set and is finite for smooth fields. With these variations on the fixed background, the intended Euler–Lagrange equations are $(\Box-\mu^2)\phi_{\mathrm n}=0$ and $(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi_{\mathrm n}=0$, conditional on the exact mathematical supplier recorded as [L1] below. As the physical interpretation of this selected free model, assign the real scalar species to the bosonic symmetric Fock representation and assign the Dirac field to the particle/antiparticle CAR representation on $\mathcal H_+\oplus\overline{\mathcal H_-}$. Choose the zero-particle Fock vectors as the scalar and Dirac vacuum states. This is an adopted species and statistics assignment. The CCR/CAR and operator properties of the specified representations are mathematical model consequences; they do not prove a general spin-statistics theorem or establish that nature realizes this model. The scalar construction is the Schwartz-smeared field $\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu\overline f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f)$ on the finite-particle domain, with the future-shell phase $p\circ x=\omega_\mu x^0-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x$, exactly as in [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. The Dirac construction is the bounded spacetime-smeared CAR field of [[lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality]], using the positive and negative projections of the specified free Dirac matrix. In that carrier, $\mathcal H_D=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k/(2\pi)^3;\mathbb C^4)$, $h_D(\mathbf k)=\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf k+\beta\mu$, and $P_\pm(\mathbf k)=(I_4\pm h_D(\mathbf k)/\omega_\mu(\mathbf k))/2$; the particle and antiparticle one-particle spaces are the closed ranges $\mathcal H_+$ and $\overline{\mathcal H_-}$. These carriers state their mathematical hypotheses and construction domains; their draft status is not an independent physics or proof approval. Tong's lecture notes and Srednicki's book draft provide independent presentations of the scalar and Dirac free-field formulations. Their formal mode notation supplies context for this adoption, not a proof of the operator-domain claims and not evidence that the adopted model describes nature.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following statement. > For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by > $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that > $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], as in the inspected Fock construction. Select the real-scalar branch of the QFT-F01 physical adoption [[post-qft-free-field-model]]: one real spin-zero species with bosonic statistics and the zero-particle vacuum. For a smooth real classical field $\phi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4	o\mathbb R$ of canonical length degree $-1$, that postulate adopts $$ rac{S_\phi}{\hbar}=- rac12\int_{\mathbb R^4} \left(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\phi_{\mathrm n}\partial_b\phi_{\mathrm n} +\mu^2\phi_{\mathrm n}^2ight)\,d^4x.$$ The species, statistics, state, and action are physical model inputs. The present item fixes the exact flat-spacetime free Fock model to which the later deductions apply. Use the oriented and time-oriented Minkowski spacetime, signature $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and $\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3$ from [[def-qft-framework-units]]. Write $\Box=-\partial_0^2+\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_j^2$. Choose an inverse-length parameter $\mu\ge0$. When $\mu>0$, the corresponding SI rest mass is $m_{\mathrm{rest,SI}}=\hbar\mu/c>0$; $\mu=0$ denotes the massless branch and assigns no positive rest mass. For $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, put $\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$, with units $\mathrm m^{-1}$. Let $H_\mu^+$, $d
u_\mu$, $H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d
u_\mu;\mathbb C)$, and $K_\mu:\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)	o H_\mu$ be the future mass shell, measure, one-particle Hilbert space, and Fourier restriction of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. In the massless case the null apex is omitted; it has measure zero. The shell measure is $d
u_\mu=d^3\mathbf k/((2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k))$. Use the symmetric bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(H_\mu)$, vacuum $\Omega=(1,0,0,\ldots)$, and dense finite-particle domain $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fin}}$ from [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. The Fock pairing is linear in its second variable. Creation $a^\dagger(h)$ is linear in $h$, while annihilation $a(h)$ is conjugate-linear in $h$. For $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$ define the complex-linear smeared scalar field on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fin}}$ by $$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu\overline f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f).$$ For real $f$, this is the symmetric scalar field whose self-adjoint closure and bounded Weyl functions are constructed in [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. A smeared field is a domain-qualified operator-valued distribution; the item introduces no pointwise operator $\Phi_\mu(x)$. Define $d\Gamma_s(\omega_\mu)$ on the $n$-particle sector as multiplication by $\sum_{r=1}^n\omega_\mu(\mathbf k_r)$, with value zero on the vacuum sector. The exact maximal domain is $$D(d\Gamma_s(\omega_\mu))= \left\{\Psi:\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{(H_\mu^+)^n} \left|\sum_{r=1}^n\omega_\mu(\mathbf k_r)ight|^2 |\Psi_n(\mathbf k_1,\ldots,\mathbf k_n)|^2\,d
u_\mu^n<\inftyight\}.$$ The physical Hamiltonian of this selected model is the vacuum-subtracted self-adjoint operator $H_\mu^{\mathrm{phys}}=\hbar c\,d\Gamma_s(\omega_\mu)$ on that domain, as defined by the multiplier construction of [[lem-qft-second-quantized-spectrum]]. It has units of joules and $H_\mu^{\mathrm{phys}}\Omega=0$. No infinite zero-point-energy sum is part of this definition. The canonical scalar engineering dimension is $\mathrm m^{-1}$; a spacetime test function of unit $\mathrm m^{-3}$ makes the smeared field dimensionless, consistently with [[def-qft-framework-units]].

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], let $\mu\ge0$, let $H_\mu$ and $K_\mu$ be as in [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]], and form $\mathcal F_s(H_\mu)$ with vacuum $\Omega$ and finite-particle domain $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ define on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ $$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu\overline f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f).$$ This is a complex-linear map of test functions into operators $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\to\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. For real $f$ it is symmetric and equals $\sqrt2\,\Phi_{\rm Segal}(K_\mu f)|_{\mathcal D_{\rm fin}}$, where the Segal field of [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]] is $\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=\overline{(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2}$. Thus its Weyl unitary is $W_\mu(f):=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2 K_\mu f)$ and, for real $f,g$, $$W_\mu(f)W_\mu(g)= e^{-i\,\operatorname{Im}\langle K_\mu f,K_\mu g\rangle_2}W_\mu(f+g).$$ For every real $f$ the vacuum Weyl expectation is $$\langle\Omega,W_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2 =e^{-\|K_\mu f\|_2^2/2}.$$ Here the inner product is second-variable-linear as fixed in [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. The vacuum has zero one-point function and two-point function $$\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(f)\Phi_\mu(g)\Omega\rangle_2 =\langle K_\mu\overline f,K_\mu g\rangle_2,$$ which obeys $\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(\overline f)\Phi_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2=\|K_\mu f\|_2^2\ge0$ for every complex test $f$ (ordinary diagonal positivity holds for real tests); higher vacuum moments of ordered real smeared fields obey the CCR pairing recursion and hence the free-field Wick pairing rule. The field is a weak operator-valued tempered distribution on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$: every matrix coefficient $f\mapsto\langle\Psi,\Phi_\mu(f)\Theta\rangle_2$ for $\Psi,\Theta\in\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is a continuous complex-linear functional on Schwartz space. Its adjoint satisfies $\Phi_\mu(f)^*|_{\mathcal D_{\rm fin}}=\Phi_\mu(\overline f)$, and its normalized vacuum defines a positive state on the finite polynomial $*$-algebra generated by these fields. The relative-coordinate two-point tempered distribution is $$W_\mu(z)=\int_{H_\mu^+}e^{-ip\circ z}\,d\nu_\mu(p),$$ understood by pairing with Schwartz tests. Its translation-invariant bidistribution is the shell integral of $e^{-ip\circ x}e^{ip\circ y}$; on product tests it is the displayed vacuum covariance. For $g=(a,\Lambda)$, let $f_g$ and $U_\mu(g)$ be the affine test pullback and one-particle action of [[lem-qft-scalar-poincare-action]]. Their Fock lifts implement the same covariance for $\Phi_\mu$ on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ and for the bounded Weyl operators. For translations, the joint spectral measure on Fock space is the second-quantized multiplier measure with one-particle vector $(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),-\mathbf k)$. Its support is contained in the closed future cone $\{(E,\mathbf P):E\ge|\mathbf P|\}$; the vacuum is an eigenvector at $(0,\mathbf0)$. These are conditional mathematical model deductions. No point field, empirical observation or measurement claim is made.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space with the second-variable-linear convention of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]], and let $\mathcal F_s(H)$ and $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ be its bosonic Fock space and finite-particle domain. For $h\in H$ define on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ the Segal field $$\phi_0(h):=2^{-1/2}\bigl(a^\dagger(h)+a(h)\bigr).$$ For $h\ne0$, this symmetric operator is essentially self-adjoint; write $\Phi(h)=\overline{\phi_0(h)}$. If $r=\|h\|$, $e=h/r$, $K=e^\perp$, $G=\mathcal F_s(K)$, choose a countable orthonormal basis $(u_j)$ of $G$ whose vectors are finite-particle, and use the one-mode splitting of [[lem-qft-fock-one-mode-splitting]] followed by the Hermite unitary $|n\rangle\mapsto g_n$ into $L^2(\mathbb R,dx;\mathbb C)$ with pairing $\langle f,g\rangle_2=\int\overline f g$ to write a vector as $(f_j)_{j\in J}\in\ell^2(J;L^2(\mathbb R,dx;\mathbb C))$. Then the exact domain and action are $$D(\Phi(h))=\left\{(f_j):\sum_{j\in J}\int_{\mathbb R}(1+r^2x^2)|f_j(x)|^2\,dx<\infty\right\},\qquad (\Phi(h)f)_j(x)=rx f_j(x).$$ For $h=0$, $\phi_0(0)$ closes to the zero operator on all of $\mathcal F_s(H)$. Define $\epsilon(z)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}z^{\otimes n}/\sqrt{n!}$ for $z\in H$. There are unitaries $W(h)$ determined on these total exponential vectors by $$W(h)\epsilon(z)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{\|h\|^2}{4} +\frac{i}{\sqrt2}\langle h,z\rangle_2\right) \epsilon\!\left(z+\frac{i h}{\sqrt2}\right).$$ They obey $$W(h)W(k)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i}{2}\operatorname{Im}\langle h,k\rangle_2\right)W(h+k),\qquad \langle\Omega,W(h)\Omega\rangle_2=e^{-\|h\|^2/4},$$ and $h\mapsto W(h)$ is strongly continuous. For every $h$, the one-parameter group $t\mapsto W(th)$ has norm derivative at zero exactly on $D(\Phi(h))$, with derivative $i\Phi(h)$ (for $h=0$ this is the zero generator). Thus the displayed bounded Weyl operators have precisely the closed Segal fields as their generators; no point-field or measurement claim is included.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Fix the scalar shell parameter $\mu\ge0$ and all shell, Fourier, and metric conventions of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]], with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\Box=-\partial_t^2+\Delta_{\mathbf x}$. For $\phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$ define the partial spatial Fourier transform $$\widehat\phi_t(\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\phi(t,\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x$$ and define $H_\mu\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$ by $$\langle H_\mu,\phi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R}dt\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)}e^{-i\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)|t|}\widehat\phi_t(-\mathbf k).$$ This is a continuous distributional extension of the free scalar time-ordered two-point function: on $t>0$ its kernel is the Wightman two-point distribution $W_\mu(t,\mathbf x)$, and on $t<0$ it is $W_\mu(-t,-\mathbf x)$. The displayed partial Fourier formula fixes the extension at $t=0$; no product of a step function with an unspecified singular distribution is used. The kernel is symmetric under $(t,\mathbf x)\mapsto(-t,-\mathbf x)$, agrees with the two orderings on spacelike-separated supports, and obeys $$ (\Box-\mu^2)H_\mu=i\delta_0 $$ in $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$. There is no extra prefactor $i$ in the definition of $H_\mu$.

Assume the scalar model adoption planned in [[post-qft-free-field-model]] and Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $\mu\ge0$ and use the model, shell, field, vacuum, and units of [[def-qft-free-scalar-model]] and [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. These are conditional model deductions, with no empirical premise. For every Schwartz test $f$, $\Phi_\mu(f)$ is defined on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fin}}$; for real $f$ it is symmetric and essentially self-adjoint there. Distributionally, $\Phi_\mu((\Box-\mu^2)f)=0$. The Fock lift of the proper orthochronous Poincare action is unitary, leaves $\Omega$ invariant, and implements covariance of the smeared field. For real Schwartz tests the vacuum two-point form is $\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(f)\Phi_\mu(g)\Omega\rangle=\langle K_\mu f,K_\mu g\rangle_2$, and it is nonnegative when $g=f$. The joint spectrum of spacetime translations is contained in the closed forward cone. For real compactly supported smooth tests with pairwise spacelike-separated supports, the smeared fields commute on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fin}}$. The bounded local Weyl algebras are isotonic and algebras for spacelike-separated regions commute. The physical Hamiltonian is self-adjoint on the exact multiplier domain in [[def-qft-free-scalar-model]], is nonnegative, and has $\Omega$ as its unique zero-energy vector. If $\mu>0$, the infimum of its positive spectrum is $\hbar c\mu=m_{\mathrm{rest,SI}}c^2$. If $\mu=0$, its positive spectrum has no gap above zero.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Here $\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ is the Schwartz space of smooth complex functions whose coordinate-weighted derivatives are all bounded, as defined in [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]. Fix an oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski space and an inertial coordinate chart as in [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]. Use coordinates $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$ and metric $\eta=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, matching the $(-+++)$ convention of the SR suppliers. Some QFT sources use its negative $(+---)$; the Lorentz group is unchanged, and the phase is fixed explicitly below. Coordinates $x$ have length units, momenta have inverse-length units, and the Fourier phase below is dimensionless. A parameter $\mu\ge0$ has inverse-length units and is only a mathematical shell parameter; it is not identified with a physical rest mass. For $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, set $$\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2},\qquad p_\mu(\mathbf k)=(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k).$$ The future mass shell is $$H_\mu^+=\{(p^0,\mathbf p): (p^0)^2-|\mathbf p|^2=\mu^2,\ p^0>0\}.$$ When $\mu=0$, its apex is omitted; thus $\mathbf k
e0$ in the massless parameterization. The scalar shell pairing is $$p\circ x:=p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x=-\eta(p,x).$$ Define the measure and one-particle Hilbert space by $$d
u_\mu(p_\mu(\mathbf k))=  rac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)},\qquad H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d
u_\mu;\mathbb C),$$ where the omitted massless apex has measure zero. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ define its pointwise shell Fourier restriction by $$K_\mu f(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}f(x)e^{ip\circ x}\,d^4x.$$ The Fourier convention is exactly the displayed integral, with no prefactor. If $\widehat f(\xi^0, oldsymbol\xi)= \int f(x)e^{-2\pi i(x^0\xi^0+\mathbf x\cdot oldsymbol\xi)}\,d^4x$ denotes the standard transform in [[cor-fourier-transform-is-a-topological-automorphism-of-schwartz-space]], then $$\mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p):=\int f(x)e^{i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)}\,d^4x =\widehat f\!\left(- rac{p^0}{2\pi}, rac{\mathbf p}{2\pi}ight).$$ Its inverse is $$f(x)=(2\pi)^{-4}\int_{\mathbb R^4} \mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p)e^{-i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)} \,dp^0\,d^3\mathbf p.$$ Thus this convention is a time reflection and rescaling of the cited Schwartz automorphism and has the stated reciprocal normalization. The proper orthochronous Lorentz group consists of linear maps preserving $\eta$, orientation and the chosen future cone. A Poincare map is $x\mapsto a+\Lambda x$ with $a\in\mathbb R^4$ and $\Lambda$ in that group. This is a mathematical free scalar one-particle construction. It adopts the chosen coordinates, measure and Fourier convention; it asserts no experimental observation, physical mass identification or measurement outcome.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n \ge 1$, let $S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be the unit sphere, and let $\sigma$ be the set function of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. Then $\sigma$ is a finite Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$, and for every Borel measurable $f : \mathbb R^n \to [0,\infty]$, $$\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)\,d\lambda_n(x) = \int_0^\infty \int_{S^{n-1}} f(r\omega) r^{n-1}\,d\sigma(\omega)\,dr.$$ Moreover, $\sigma$ is the unique Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$ with this property.

Let $n \ge 1$, **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice** ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $T : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be linear with matrix $A$ ([[def-linear-map]], [[lem-euclidean-linear-maps-have-matrices-and-are-bounded]]). 1. **Invertible case.** If $\det A \ne 0$, then $T[E]$ is Lebesgue measurable for every Lebesgue measurable $E$ and $$\lambda_n\big(T[E]\big) \;=\; |\det A|\;\lambda_n(E),$$ both sides possibly $+\infty$; the product is defined in $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ because $|\det A| > 0$. 2. **Singular case.** If $\det A = 0$, then $T[E]$ is Lebesgue measurable with $\lambda_n(T[E]) = 0$ for **every** $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$. **The singular clause is stated as nullity and not as a product.** When $\det A = 0$ and $\lambda_n(E) = +\infty$ the expression $|\det A|\,\lambda_n(E)$ is $0\cdot(+\infty)$, which [[def-extended-reals]] leaves undefined; writing the conclusion as $\lambda_n(T[E]) = 0$ says the same thing wherever the product is defined and remains a statement where it is not.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $n \ge 1$ and write $$S^{n-1}:=\{\omega \in \mathbb R^n : |\omega|=1\}.$$ Let $$\Phi:\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\longrightarrow(0,\infty)\times S^{n-1},\qquad \Phi(x)=(|x|,x/|x|).$$ This map is continuous. If $E\subseteq S^{n-1}$ is Borel, then $(0,1]\times E$ is Borel and $$\{r\omega:\omega\in E,\ 0<r\le1\}=\Phi^{-1}((0,1]\times E)$$ is Borel in $\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$ by [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]], hence Borel in $\mathbb R^n$ by [[thm-borel-sigma-algebra-of-a-subspace-is-the-trace]]. It is therefore Lebesgue measurable by [[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]. Define $$\sigma(E):=n\,\lambda_n(\{r\omega : \omega \in E,\ 0<r\le 1\}).$$ The next theorem proves that this is a Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$ and that it is exactly the surface measure needed for polar coordinates.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ and let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on $S^2$ of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], a finite Borel measure ([[def-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Let $$\Phi:(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)\to S^2,\qquad \Phi(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta),$$ and let $H:=\{(x,y,0)\in\mathbb R^3:x\ge0\}$ denote the closed half-plane, a Lebesgue-null Borel set ([[thm-affine-hyperplanes-and-proper-subspaces-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]). Then: (a) for every Borel function $F:S^2\to[0,+\infty]$, $$\int_{S^2}F\,d\sigma=\int_{(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)}F\bigl(\Phi(\theta,\varphi)\bigr)\,\sin\theta\ d(\theta,\varphi),$$ the right-hand integral being the Lebesgue integral over the open rectangle; (b) $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$; (c) the identity of (a) holds with $F\in L^1(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$ in the sense that $F\circ\Phi$ is Lebesgue integrable on the rectangle against $\sin\theta\,d(\theta,\varphi)$ and the two integrals agree (real and imaginary parts, positive and negative parts).
